note: Lesson 7.1 (discovery) has no workflow build: its solved problem is a signed requirements document.

walk.title: Solve it: from a messy office to a signed requirements document
walk.sample: Kora Properties, Lekki and Ibadan · 400 enquiries a month · 11 spreadsheets

steps.say: Kora Properties loses enquiries between portals, Instagram and eleven spreadsheets. Before we open any CRM, we find out how deals really move and agree what success means.
Workshop one, ninety minutes. Mrs Adeyemi, two senior agents, a new agent and the administrator walk the last won sale and the last lost rental on sticky notes.
Now the numbers. About four hundred enquiries a month, over half from the portals. The median first reply is six hours, and forty hours at weekends.
The data audit. Of eighteen thousand four hundred rows, a third are duplicates. Only about four thousand three hundred people were active in the last two years.
So the decision: migrate active people, open deals and available properties, and archive the rest as a read-only export.
Workshop two plays the map back with the leaks marked. The agents correct it, and everyone agrees the success measures.
show: Every enquiry owned within 1 working hour

steps.say: Prioritise with MoSCoW: twelve musts, six shoulds, four coulds, three won'ts. Routing, workflows and team permissions rule out a free plan.
show: Compare two paid plans for 12 users, priced on the day

steps.say: Write it in eight pages at most, present it in thirty minutes, and get it signed in the room or within a week.
show: Platform and yearly cost · out of scope · risks

walk.end: That's discovery: real deals mapped, the data measured, success agreed, and a signed document before anything is built.
